open_questions.question: Exact nature of EB - fully on target vs diluted by neighbour - inconclusive centroid (verdict inconclusive, diff_snr 1.577, centroid_all not_run) needs ground-based photometry/spectroscopy.

dossier.public_summary: The TESS dips alternate between deep and shallow every orbit and change depth by more than a factor of two between sectors, which is the signature of a binary eclipsing at about twice the reported period rather than a planet. The low planet score and inconsistent transit depths confirm this is not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Odd transits are about 2.9x deeper (7354 ppm) than even (2522 ppm) with 5.9 sigma difference - positive evidence for an eclipsing binary at twice the 10.4 d period, not a planet.

Depth changes by ~120% between sectors and sector_depths_by_source verdict is changes_within_a_source, confirmed not a calibration difference - primary and secondary of a binary seen in different sectors at different phases.
reasons.value: p_constant 2.357e-14 depth_change_pct 116.9; sector 46 TESS-SPOC 2336 +/-492 ppm vs sector 91 QLP 8905 +/-707 ppm

reasons.why: Low planet score supports binary interpretation; combined with stable odd/even sign share 1.0 and sector_oe_max_sigma 4.654, the signal is best explained as a blended or target EB masquerading at 10.4 d.
